cards.title: Contract of the closed schemas and of the data sent to the billing provider
cards.body: Scope: write the contract of the new pricing page of Acme Notes before any code. Steps: 1) describe the closed schema of a plan (name, monthly and yearly price, seats, limits) and of an upgrade request; 2) list exactly which fields leave for the billing provider, and which never do; 3) keep the change behind the existing module boundaries and add no dependency; 4) cover the nominal case, each refusal and one malformed input with a test; 5) log nothing that identifies a user or the content of a note; 6) write the short note of the choices made, next to the code; 7) run the whole test suite before handing over. Out of scope: the interface, the visual design, any change of infrastructure. Acceptance criteria: the tests pass, extra fields are refused, each refusal has its own code and no behaviour outside the scope changes. Proof: the real output of the test run and the list of the files changed.

cards.title: Static mock-up of the pricing page and of the upgrade dialog
cards.body: Scope: a static page in mockups/pricing.html, with no logic and no call. Steps: 1) draw the three plans Free, Plus and Team, the monthly or yearly switch and the comparison table; 2) draw every state of the upgrade dialog (choice, summary, error, limit reached, done); 3) check the result at 380 px and 1440 px, with the keyboard and with a pointer; 4) leave no error or warning in the console of the browser; 5) respect the reduced-motion preference for anything that moves; 6) run the build and the tests before handing over; 7) keep the existing components and class names where they already do the job. Out of scope: the API, the content, a redesign of the screens that are not named. Acceptance criteria: no regression of the existing screens, keyboard use works end to end and the console stays empty. Proof: the diff, the output of the tests and before and after screenshots.

cards.title: Visual critique of the mock-up
cards.body: Scope: judge the real rendering of the mock-up before the human validation. Steps: 1) open mockups/pricing.html in a browser and capture each state at 360 px and 1280 px; 2) compare with the design system of the app and judge hierarchy, typography, colours and the legibility of the prices; 3) say for each finding what would fix it, in one precise sentence; 4) compare with the reference of the project and name the gap; 5) end with one clear verdict. Out of scope: changing the code or the mock-up yourself, writing copy. Acceptance criteria: every finding is located, measured and comes with a precise recommendation, and the verdict is unambiguous. Proof: a report with the annotated screenshots.

cards.title: Interface copy in English, French and Spanish for the page and the dialog
cards.body: Scope: write every text of the pricing page and of the upgrade dialog in the three languages, from the mock-up. Steps: 1) collect each label, help text, error message and confirmation of mockups/pricing.html; 2) produce a table key, en, fr, es in docs/i18n-pricing.md with stable keys; 3) read the text once more against the real behaviour; 4) list what could not be verified; 5) write from what can be checked in the code, the data or the briefs, and invent nothing; 6) follow the tone and the format of the existing texts of the project. Out of scope: the layout of the pages, the technical integration. Acceptance criteria: each text answers its brief, no sentence is invented and the lengths fit where they go. Proof: the texts, with for each one the brief or the source it comes from.

cards.title: Review of the scoping: contract, mock-up, copy
cards.body: Scope: validate the scoping before the human validation of the mock-up. Steps: 1) read docs/pricing-contract.md and check that the schemas are closed and that the list of data sent is complete and minimal; 2) check that each state of the contract is in the mock-up and that the copy matches its labels; 3) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked; 4) measure it yourself instead of trusting the report of the card. Out of scope: rewriting the deliverable, widening the scope of the card reviewed. Acceptance criteria: a global verdict with numbered findings, each one reproducible, and nothing validated that was not checked. Proof: the review report with the real output of the build and of the tests.

cards.title: Backend: plans.py, API routes, seat limit, pytest tests
cards.body: Scope: the server side of the pricing page, in api/billing, from the validated contract. Steps: 1) implement the route that lists the plans and the one that records an upgrade request; 2) enforce the seat limit of each plan on the server and test it with a fake billing client; 3) keep the change behind the existing module boundaries and add no dependency; 4) cover the nominal case, each refusal and one malformed input with a test; 5) log nothing that identifies a user or the content of a note; 6) write the short note of the choices made, next to the code. Out of scope: the web pages, the copy, the deployment. Acceptance criteria: the contract is respected field by field, the tests cover each rule and the suite is green. Proof: the diff, the output of the tests and one example of each answer.

cards.title: Pure logic in web/core: price computation, validation, node tests
cards.body: Scope: the pure functions of the page, with no network and no DOM. Steps: 1) compute the price shown for a plan, a period and a number of seats, rounding included; 2) validate an upgrade request against the contract before it is sent; 3) check the result at 380 px and 1440 px, with the keyboard and with a pointer; 4) leave no error or warning in the console of the browser; 5) respect the reduced-motion preference for anything that moves. Out of scope: the server code, the copy of the interface, any new dependency. Acceptance criteria: the build passes, the rendering matches the reference on every screen named and nothing shifts while the page loads. Proof: the output of the build and screenshots of each state at both widths.

cards.title: Review of the backend and of the pure logic
cards.body: Scope: the diff of the cards c6 and c7. Steps: 1) check that the schemas of the code are the ones of the contract, field by field; 2) run pytest and the node tests, and try a request with an extra field; 3) look for a regression next to the change, not only in it; 4) number each finding and say how to reproduce it; 5) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked; 6) measure it yourself instead of trusting the report of the card. Out of scope: fixing what you find yourself. Acceptance criteria: every criterion of the card reviewed is checked one by one and the verdict follows from the findings. Proof: the numbered findings and the commands that were run.

cards.title: Web page: PricingPage faithful to the validated mock-up
cards.body: Scope: the page web/pages/PricingPage, built on the pure logic of c7. Steps: 1) render the three plans, the switch of period and the comparison table from the plan list of the API; 2) handle loading, an empty list and an error without a layout shift; 3) respect the reduced-motion preference for anything that moves; 4) run the build and the tests before handing over. Out of scope: the server code, the copy of the interface, any new dependency. Acceptance criteria: the build passes, the rendering matches the reference on every screen named and nothing shifts while the page loads. Proof: the output of the build and screenshots of each state at both widths.

cards.title: Web page: UpgradeDialog faithful to the validated mock-up
cards.body: Scope: the dialog web/pages/UpgradeDialog, opened from a plan of the page. Steps: 1) show the plan, the seats and the summary with the price computed by the pure logic; 2) send the request only on the confirmation click and show each refusal in plain words; 3) run the build and the tests before handing over; 4) keep the existing components and class names where they already do the job; 5) check the result at 380 px and 1440 px, with the keyboard and with a pointer. Out of scope: the API, the content, a redesign of the screens that are not named. Acceptance criteria: no regression of the existing screens, keyboard use works end to end and the console stays empty. Proof: the diff, the output of the tests and before and after screenshots.

cards.title: Review of the web pages
cards.body: Scope: the diff of the cards c9 and c10. Steps: 1) compare the page and the dialog with the mock-up, state by state; 2) check that nothing is sent before the click; 3) measure it yourself instead of trusting the report of the card; 4) run the build and the tests again and quote their real output; 5) look for a regression next to the change, not only in it. Out of scope: rewriting the deliverable, widening the scope of the card reviewed. Acceptance criteria: a global verdict with numbered findings, each one reproducible, and nothing validated that was not checked. Proof: the review report with the real output of the build and of the tests.

cards.title: Security audit: data sent to the billing provider and what comes back
cards.body: Scope: the routes of api/billing and the two pages. Steps: 1) trace every field that leaves the server and compare it with the list of the contract; 2) try injected markup in a plan name and a forged number of seats, and look for a secret in the logs; 3) stay inside the test environment and exploit nothing outside it; 4) check the logs and the error messages for a secret or a personal detail; 5) read the dependencies added by the change; 6) say for each finding what closes it; 7) give each finding a severity and a proof that can be replayed. Out of scope: any change of infrastructure, any real payment. Acceptance criteria: nothing leaves the server that the contract does not list and no secret appears anywhere. Proof: the findings, their proofs and the list of what was checked.

cards.title: Browser acceptance and non-regression tests
cards.body: Scope: the pricing page and the upgrade dialog in a real browser, in the three languages. Steps: 1) run the journeys compare, choose a plan, change the seats, confirm and cancel; 2) write the missing non-regression tests for the limit and for the error states; 3) give each bug its steps, what was expected and what happened; 4) check the keyboard, both themes and three screen widths; 5) keep the tests that were written in the suite of the project. Out of scope: fixing the bugs, judging the visual design. Acceptance criteria: every journey has a result, every bug can be reproduced from its steps and the new tests run in the suite. Proof: the test report, the output of the suite and a screenshot per bug.

cards.title: Final review: audit, acceptance and criteria of the project
cards.body: Scope: the findings of c12 and c13 and the state of the branch. Steps: 1) check that each finding has a fix or a written justification; 2) run the build and every test suite again and give the verdict; 3) number each finding and say how to reproduce it; 4) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked; 5) measure it yourself instead of trusting the report of the card; 6) run the build and the tests again and quote their real output. Out of scope: fixing what you find yourself. Acceptance criteria: every criterion of the card reviewed is checked one by one and the verdict follows from the findings. Proof: the numbered findings and the commands that were run.
